USAGE:
    opentail-llm-cli gguf-transplant <OPTIONS>

    Build a mixed-precision GGUF by copying a base checkpoint and taking selected tensors (regex)
    from a donor checkpoint; verifies the result byte-for-byte

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help  Prints help information
    --base      GGUF whose header, metadata and (non-replaced) tensors are kept
    --donor     GGUF supplying the replacement tensors (same tensor names and dimensions as the
                base)
    --tensors   Regex matched against base tensor names; matching tensors are taken from the donor
    -o, --out   Output GGUF path (must not be the base or donor; must not exist unless --force)
    --force     Overwrite the output if it exists
    --dry-run   Print the replacement plan and the resulting size, write nothing

USAGE:
    opentail-llm-cli plan <OPTIONS>

    Read-only GGUF compatibility, hardware availability, and placement plan report

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help                Prints help information
    -m, --model <PATH>        Path to a GGUF model file
    --profile <PATH>          Optional JSON planning profile; CLI values override profile,
                              environment, then defaults
    --save-profile <PATH>     Write the resolved strict planning profile; may be used without a
                              model
    --backend <NAME>          Backend preference: auto, cpu, cuda, or vulkan
    --device <NAME>           Requested device (none forces CPU; a named/indexed GPU is reported but
                              not selected by inspect)
    --target <NAME>           Eligibility target: cli (default) or server
    -g, --gpu-layers <N>      GPU layers: 0 = CPU, -1 = planner-selected, omitted = default 0
    -c, --ctx-size <N>        Context size (0 = planner/model default)
    --tq <BOOL>               Whether TurboQuant KV compression is requested
    --tq-mode <NAME>          TurboQuant mode: auto, kvarn, or lloydmax
    --kv-type <NAME>          KV element type: fp32, bf16, or q8_0
    --spec-type <NAME>        Speculation type: auto, none, or mtp
    --max-batch <N>           Requested maximum batch size
    --tool-grammar <BOOL>     Whether tool grammar is requested
    --no-gpu-probe            Do not initialize CUDA/Vulkan; report GPU availability as not probed
    --json                    Write machine-readable JSON to stdout
    --print-effective-config  Print the resolved planning configuration and exit; a model is not
                              required
    --print-profile-schema    Write the strict JSON Schema for --profile and exit; a model is not
                              required
    --explain                 Include the full selected/rejected decision trace in text output

USAGE:
    opentail-llm-cli perplexity <OPTIONS>

    Teacher-forced perplexity over a text file (llama.cpp llama-perplexity analogue; CPU only).
    Reports mean NLL, perplexity, and position-bucket NLLs â the TurboQuant/KVarN accuracy gate
    (issue #180).

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help                               Prints help information
    -m, --model                              Path to GGUF model file
    -f, --file                               UTF-8 text file to evaluate (llama.cpp -f/--file).
                                             Tokenized raw (no chat template); the first -c tokens
                                             are scored.
    -c, --ctx-size                           Number of tokens to evaluate (default: 2048). Clamped
                                             to the model context length and the corpus length.
    --tq                                     Enable TurboQuant KV cache compression (same flag as
                                             the run command) (default: False)
    --tq-mode                                TurboQuant quantizer for --tq: auto (default: kvarn
                                             where supported, else lloydmax with a quality warning),
                                             kvarn (issue #180: 4-bit K / 2-bit V, 128-token tiles),
                                             or lloydmax (3-bit codebooks; severely degrades quality
                                             on QK-norm models such as Qwen3 — issue #432).
    --tq-window                              FP32 recent-token window before compression kicks in
                                             (default: 256; min 128 for kvarn — one full tile). Also
                                             sets the first position-bucket edge of the report, so
                                             pass the same value to the fp32 baseline for
                                             bucket-comparable numbers.
    --ngl, --n-gpu-layers, --gpu-layers, -g  Layers on GPU: 0

    paths.

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help                               Prints help information
    -m, --model                              Path to diffusion model GGUF or safetensors directory
                                             (FLUX.1, Z-Image-Turbo, …)
    -p, --prompt                             Text prompt describing the image to generate
    --negative-prompt                        Negative prompt — what to avoid in the generated image
    --vae                                    Path to VAE safetensors file or directory
                                             (ae.safetensors or vae/ dir)
    --qwen-encoder                           (Z-Image) Path to Qwen3-4B GGUF text encoder (from
                                             Qwen/Qwen3-4B-GGUF)
    --qwen-tokenizer                         (Z-Image) Path to Qwen3 tokenizer.json
    --umt5-encoder                           (Wan) Path to the real UMT5-XXL text encoder
                                             safetensors (converted from Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B's
                                             models_t5_umt5-xxl-enc-bf16.pth)
    --umt5-tokenizer                         (Wan) Path to the real UMT5 tokenizer.json
                                             (Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B's
                                             google/umt5-xxl/tokenizer.json)
    --ngl, --n-gpu-layers, --gpu-layers, -g  (Z-Image) GPU acceleration: -1 = auto (CUDA→Vulkan→CPU,
                                             default), 0 = CPU only
    --device                                 (Z-Image) GPU to use: auto (default), none/cpu, an
                                             index (0, 1), or a named device (CUDA0, Vulkan1)
    --backend                                (Z-Image) Force compute backend: auto (default),

                           segments.

USAGE:
    opentail-llm-cli capture-golden <OPTIONS>

    Capture a golden reference from the vendored llama.cpp: oracle-tokenized prompt ids, greedy
    continuation from llama-server, model SHA-256; writes a small JSON with no machine paths. Check
    it later with admit-arch --golden.

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help                  Prints help information
    -m, --model <PATH>          GGUF to capture a reference for
    --prompt <TEXT>             Raw prompt text, tokenized by llama-tokenize (the model's own BOS
                                behaviour applies)
    --prompt-ids <IDS>          Comma-separated prompt token ids, used as-is instead of tokenizing
                                --prompt
    -n, --tokens <N>            Tokens to generate
    --mode <MODE>               How the golden is checked later: free (greedy run compared until it
                                diverges) or teacherForced (reference tokens fed, every position
                                compared)
    --case <NAME>               Name of this case inside the golden (an existing case of the same
                                name is replaced)
    -o, --out <PATH>            Golden file to write (default: ./<architecture>.golden.json); an
                                existing file for the same model gets the case added
    --source <REPO>             Where the checkpoint came from (Hugging Face repo id), recorded in
                                the golden
    --notes <TEXT>              Provenance notes recorded in the golden (no paths: the file is
                                checked for machine-specific text)
    --server <EXE>              llama-server executable (default: tools/llama.cpp/llama-server.exe
                                found upward from here)
    --tokenizer <EXE>           llama-tokenize executable (default:
                                tools/llama.cpp/llama-tokenize.exe found upward from here)
    --threads <N>
    --ctx-size <N>
    --server-timeout <SECONDS>  How long to wait for llama-server

    -m, --model <PATH>       Path to a GGUF model file
    -r, --repo <ID>          Inspect a model on Hugging Face instead of a local file, e.g.
                             bartowski/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-GGUF. Reads only the index with Range
                             requests; the weights are never downloaded. Subject to
                             STINGRAY_ALLOW_EXTERNAL.
    -f, --file <NAME>        With --repo: which GGUF in the repo (file name, path, or the base name
                             of a split model). Needed when the repo has several.
    --revision <REV>         With --repo: commit, branch or tag to inspect (default: the current
                             head). The report records the exact commit.
    --quants                 With --repo: judge EVERY quantisation in the repo against this machine
                             instead of one file: reads each file's index (a few MB each, no
                             weights), applies the memory gate, and prints which fit with a pull
                             command pinned to the inspected commit. Budget defaults to this
                             machine's RAM.
    --max-quants <N>         With --quants: most files to inspect (default 40, largest first).
    --max-index-mb <N>       With --repo: most MB of a file's header and tensor index to read
                             (default 128). Past it the report says the inspection is incomplete;
                             nothing more is fetched.
    --format <FORMAT>        Output format: text (default) or json
    -o, --output <PATH>      Write the JSON report to this file (in addition to the chosen stdout
                             format)
    --budget <SIZE>          Host RAM budge
